entities.span: **The two AC-16 clauses this spec amended on 2026-09-06, kept verbatim so the change is auditable.**
rejected_spans: Both were written at design time and neither was reachable from a test in this repo, which is why both survived to `/check verify`.

entities.span: "a single polite `aria-live` region announces once, when the one time re-sort in AC-9 happens, that results are now ranked"
rejected_spans: which was true of the happy path and false of a batch that ranked nothing

entities.span: "the re-sort never moves keyboard focus away from whatever the reader was focused on"
rejected_spans: which no implementation could satisfy: the reveal destroys the node, so focus is always moved and the only question is whether it is given back

entities.span: **The announcement fix landed in code before the spec said so, and that order is backwards.** `/debug` shipped it on 2026-09-06 and correctly did not rewrite this spec, but nothing in the flow then forced the spec back into agreement; this run did it by hand. If that gap recurs, the fix is a rule about who reconciles a spec after `/debug`, not a bigger `/debug`.

**AC-2's own evidence is now partly in hand and it is not encouraging.** Two live scored renders on 2026-09-06 spread across three and four of the five bands, so the bands do discriminate. But the same visible condition, an excerpt naming no requirements at all, produced `strong_match` on three cards in one render and `possible_match` on six in the same render. Feature 16's harness should be pointed at that specific inconsistency, not only at whether the spread exists. And 16 of 20 cards showed no matched skills at all, which is correct against a 500 character excerpt but means the chips carry very little of the "shown work" this feature is named for; the written reasoning is doing nearly all of it.
Verify OpenAI's terms on training and retention for API submitted content before this feature ships against real profile data in production.
rejected_spans: This is scope.md's own diligence owed to feature 14, carried forward unchanged; the vendor named is OpenAI, not Anthropic, per spec 0012's 2026-09-06 revision.

entities.span: **Resolved 2026-09-06, and the two halves resolved differently.** *Training*: confirmed already safe with no action. OpenAI has not used API submitted data to train or improve its models since 2023-03-01 unless a customer explicitly opts in, and nothing in this repo opts in, so the privacy notice's "not used to train models" claim stands unchanged (developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data, read 2026-09-06). *Retention*: needed a code change and got one. `ai_scoring` resolves to OpenAI's Responses API (the provider's default since AI SDK 5), whose `store` option defaults to `true`, and a stored request and response is retained as "Application State" for a minimum of 30 days. `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts` now sets `providerOptions: { openai: { store: false } }` on that tier, so a person's summary, skills and work history are no longer held for a month. Scoring is stateless per render (`## Feature design`, "State transitions": none) and makes one single step call with no tools, so nothing is lost by opting out. Locked by `src/lib/ai/tiers.test.ts`.

Feature 17 (cross vendor self check) should reuse `scoreListings()`'s concurrent dispatch pattern for its own `ai_check` calls once it is designed; this spec establishes that pattern but does not build the check itself.

If feature 16's eval harness later shows the five bands clustering rather than spreading (the condition **AC-2** defers to that harness), the band anchors in `rubric.ts` are the first thing to revise, not the vendor or any of this prompt's other instructions. **Still open, and its trigger has not fired.** Feature 16's harness ran the full sixteen pairs twice on 2026-09-08 and both runs observed all five bands, `strong_match` 35, `good_match` 5, `possible_match` 21, `weak_match` 11, `not_a_match` 8 in the first and 35, 4, 21, 8, 12 in the second, so the bands spread rather than clustered and AC-2's bar of at least three of five was already met. Spec 0018 did review the anchors, but for a different reason, two pairs disagreeing with their recorded expectation, and it concluded that `BAND_ANCHORS` holds and one committed expectation was wrong. No anchor changed and the hash is still `1b45f524b356`. So this item is neither satisfied nor superseded by that review; it is waiting on a clustering condition that has not been seen.

The fetch full posting option (`defuddle` from `job_url`) is parked, not rejected forever. Revisit it only alongside a deliberate decision to add a headless browser to this project's stack, and only after asking Adzuna directly about automated redirect fetching rather than inferring a position from their terms' silence on it.
Feature 18's own owed decision on what a repeat view of `/search` should cost also resolves this feature's repeat view cost for scoring, since both ride the same render. No separate fix is owed here.
Feature 15's ground truth set should include at least one pair that varies stated preferences (title, location, remote, pay) while holding skills and experience fixed.
rejected_spans: This feature's own instruction to keep preferences out of the band is enforced only by the prompt, not the schema (see Key invariants); without a pair built specifically to isolate preferences from skills, feature 16's eval harness has no case that could catch preference driven band contamination even in principle.

entities.span: **Resolved 2026-09-07 by feature 15, and it took two passes to cover all four dimensions.** Spec 0016's AC-4 built three `preference-isolation` tagged pairs against one archetype (`src/features/scoring/eval/pairs.ts`): `preference-match` where every stated preference agrees, `preference-violation` where location, remote language and pay all conflict at once, and `preference-title-conflict` where only the posting's title falls outside `desired_titles`. All three share one `BASELINE_REQUIREMENTS` constant, so skills and experience really are held fixed, and all three carry the same `expectedBand`, so a harness run scoring them differently is the evidence this item asked for. The title pair was missing from the first version and added on review: AC-4 originally named only three of the four dimensions this line lists, which left `desired_titles` conflicted nowhere in the set. `src/features/scoring/eval/prompt.test.ts` locks the rendered result, the title pair's prompt differing from its baseline on the `Title:` line alone.

If real usage shows the full 30 second worst case (Consequences) happens often enough to matter, add an aggregate deadline shorter than the per call timeout, after which any listing still pending renders as a failure rather than waiting out its own call.
rejected_spans: Not built now: it trades completeness for responsiveness in a way no acceptance criterion here requires, and an abandoned call still spends its `usage_cap` unit whether or not the page waits for it.

entities.span: **AC-17's rule 3 is unrunnable through the app as written, because the reason given for it is not the mechanism that makes it true.** **The guard itself is still correct and is still tested**, directly rather than through two real searches, by `focus-keeper.dom.test.tsx:269` ("forgets the key even on a mount that declined to use it"). What is owed is one of two edits, not a code change: either rewrite `verify.md`'s step 37 to describe something the app can actually be made to do, or correct the rule's stated rationale to the real mechanism, module state clearing on navigation rather than surviving a same tab second search. Until then step 37 stays unticked and unrunnable.
rejected_spans: The rule guards a focus key from one search pulling focus into the next, and reasons that "two searches in one browser tab share one module instance". They do not: `src/features/search/search-form.tsx:33` is a plain `<form method="get" action="/search">`, so every search is a full document load that re-evaluates `focus-keeper.tsx` and clears its module state. Verified 2026-09-07 and recorded in `docs/session-notes.md`.
which understates it, since the behaviour is proven and only the described route to observing it is wrong

entities.span: **AC-9 names a pairing mechanism the code does not use, and the difference is load bearing rather than cosmetic.** AC-9 and the Value sourcing table (line 100) both say outcomes are matched back to their card "by `sourceJobId`, never the array index". `ScoredResults` in `src/app/(app)/search/page.tsx:442` pairs by array index, at the one point where `scoreListings()` guarantees one outcome per listing in order, and then carries that pair through the reorder so nothing later matches on a position that has since changed. **The guarantee AC-9 exists to protect does hold**, and as of 2026-09-07 it is proven rather than assumed by `src/app/(app)/search/page.test.ts`'s pairing test, which was shown to fail when a row takes its listing from the sorted array and its outcome from the unsorted one, a break both neighbouring ordering tests pass. The difference that matters: index pairing is safe only while `scoreListings()` keeps returning one outcome per listing in order, where a `sourceJobId` keyed pairing would not depend on that guarantee at all. So this is a real choice, not just wording: correct the spec to describe index pairing before the sort, or decide the `sourceJobId` keyed pairing is genuinely wanted and change the code to match. **That choice belongs to `/architect`**, and this entry deliberately does not make it.
